title: Latch a toolbox before carrying it by its lid handle
instruction: Put the toolbox on the shelf.
context: A toolbox with its latches open looks closed, but its only handle is on the lid. Lifted by the handle, the shallow base swings down off the hinge and the tools fall out. The robot should see the two open latches, flip them shut, then carry the box. Any dropped tool scores 0.
setup: Positions are centres in cm: x forward from the arm bases, y left, from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top. Toolbox: blue plastic, 22 cm front to back, 12 cm wide, at x 30, y 10. Base: shallow tray 2.5 cm tall, 6 mm walls and floor, 120 g. Lid: deep shell 7 cm tall, 200 g, hinged along the base's back top edge (opens up to 180 degrees, swings freely). Handle: black bar on the lid top, running front to back, 11 x 1.6 x 2.4 cm, on two posts 2.2 cm tall, 9 cm apart. Two orange latch levers (2.2 cm wide, 4.2 cm long, 4 mm thick, 10 g), pivoting on the base's front face 1 cm above the table, at y 6.5 and 13.5. Closed, a lever lies flat on the box and its top hooks a steel keeper on the lid front; an over-centre spring snaps it shut over its last 30 degrees (once pushed 10 degrees from open). At the start both levers lean out 40 degrees (open) and the lid rests shut, unfastened. Inside, on the floor: a steel wrench (16 x 2.5 x 0.6 cm, 80 g) along the box at y 6.5; a yellow tape measure (5.6 cm across, 3.5 cm tall, 90 g) at x 23.5, y 12; a green tin of screws (4.4 cm across, 4.5 cm tall, 70 g) at x 36.5, y 12.5; red pliers (5 x 3 x 1.5 cm block, 70 g) at x 30, y 12.5. Total 0.65 kg. Shelf: fixed wooden platform, 28 x 20 cm, 8 cm tall, at x 30, y -13, with a 1.2 cm tall, 1 cm wide lip round its top edge (inside 26 x 18 cm). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured from the video and a ruler. 0 if any tool ever leaves the box, the box tips past 45 degrees, falls off the table, is dropped (moves down faster than 1 m/s, about a 5 cm free fall), or its lid opens more than 30 degrees while the box is off the table and the shelf. Otherwise: 0.25 one latch closed (lever flat on the box, hooked on its keeper, with the lid shut); 0.5 both closed; 0.75 both closed and the box was lifted 5 cm or more off the table with both closed; 1.0 the box at rest on the shelf, its centre inside the lip, bottom on the shelf (within 1 cm), upright within 10 degrees, lid shut (within 5 degrees), every tool inside (latched or not). In simulation, 1.0 must hold for 1 s.
reset_notes: Put the four tools back on their marks inside the base, close the lid without latching, flip both levers open against their stops, and set the box on its mark on the table. Nothing is used up.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes. Lid and latches are joints of one articulation without self-collision: the lid rests on its lower limit, latch hooks are not modelled as contacts. Code sets joint torques every physics step: a latch within 30 deg of closed is pulled shut (0.04 N m); one closed with the lid shut engages, and then a 60 N m/rad spring holds the lid shut (0.5 deg give under load).
